note: You consume the whole leaf, so it lands higher than steeped greens. Ceremonial grade with more shading tends toward the upper end.
Generally the highest of the steeped-and-strained categories, though overlap with oolong and green is substantial.
Wide range reflecting the category's wide oxidation span and highly variable brewing styles.
Lower brewing temperature extracts less caffeine, which is part of why green often feels gentler.
Commonly called low-caffeine, but bud-heavy white teas like Silver Needle can be surprisingly high — buds concentrate caffeine.
Fermentation does not meaningfully remove caffeine, despite frequent claims otherwise.
Roasting drives off a substantial share of the caffeine, making it the usual choice for evening drinking.
Not tea at all — no Camellia sinensis, so no caffeine (rooibos, chamomile, peppermint). Yerba mate and guayusa are separate caffeinated plants.
Included for comparison — a typical 8oz cup runs well above any steeped tea.
